title: Rename the pre-existing `.shinychat-*` CSS classes to the `.shiny-chat-*` prefix
description:
shinychat renders two families of CSS class names with inconsistent prefixes:

- `.shiny-chat-*` — the older, dominant convention (`.shiny-chat-container`, `.shiny-chat-message`, `.shiny-chat-input`, …).
- `.shinychat-*` (no hyphen) — a scattering of newer classes.

They should be unified on `.shiny-chat-*`.

The condensed tool-view classes (`.shinychat-tool-group*`, `.shinychat-tool-call-row*`, `.shinychat-tool-loop`, `.shinychat-tool-row__intent`, `.shinychat-tool-custom-display`, `.shinychat-tool-glyph-dot`, `.shinychat-tool-spacer`) are being renamed in #283 as they are new there and carry no back-compat cost. **This issue covers the remaining `.shinychat-*` classes, which already ship on `main`:**

- **Thinking:** `.shinychat-thinking`, `-header`, `-label`, `-topic`, `-glyph`, `-dot`, `-disclosure`, `-content`, `-content-inner`
- **PDF attachment:** `.shinychat-pdf`, `__filename`, `__icon`
- **Buttons:** `.shinychat-btn-always`, `-cancel`, `-close`, `-proceed`
- **Misc:** `.shinychat-raw-html`, `.shinychat-browser-token`, `.shinychat-link`, `.shinychat-content-extra`, `.shinychat-current`, `.shinychat-external-link-dialog`, `.shinychat-tool-image`

## Notes

- **Higher risk than the custom-property rename (#285) and than #283's new classes.** These are shipped, rendered DOM class names: authors target them in custom CSS, and unlike custom properties they cannot be cheaply aliased for back-compat. Weigh a deprecation window vs a clean break.
- Spans TypeScript/TSX (class assignments) and SCSS (selectors) in `js/src`, plus any selectors in the R/Python packages that reference these classes. Rebuild and redistribute to both packages after the rename (`npm run build`, `make py-update-dist r-update-dist`).
- Related: #285 is the custom-property half of the same inconsistency; ideally land both under one convention decision.

title: Rename `--shinychat-thinking-*` CSS custom properties to the `--shiny-chat-*` prefix
description:
The thinking display exposes three author-settable CSS custom properties under a `--shinychat-*` prefix, which is inconsistent with the rest of shinychat's public CSS API (`--shiny-chat-*`, e.g. `--shiny-chat-command-chip-color`, `--shiny-tool-card-*`, and the newly added `--shiny-chat-activity-opacity`).

The inconsistent names, all defined on `.shinychat-thinking` in `js/src/chat/chat.scss`:

- `--shinychat-thinking-header-color`
- `--shinychat-thinking-border-color`
- `--shinychat-thinking-content-color`

Proposed rename:

- `--shinychat-thinking-header-color` → `--shiny-chat-thinking-header-color`
- `--shinychat-thinking-border-color` → `--shiny-chat-thinking-border-color`
- `--shinychat-thinking-content-color` → `--shiny-chat-thinking-content-color`

## Notes

- These three properties are the only `--shinychat-*` (no hyphen) custom properties in the codebase; everything else already uses `--shiny-chat-*`.
- They are not referenced in any package documentation (R or Python), so the public exposure is real but unadvertised.
- This is a breaking change for anyone who has set the old names. Rebuild and redistribute to both packages after the rename (`npm run build`, `make py-update-dist r-update-dist`).
- Surfaced while adding `--shiny-chat-activity-opacity` (the shared tool/thinking activity-dim token), which deliberately followed the `--shiny-chat-*` convention.

## Related

The same `.shinychat-*` vs `.shiny-chat-*` inconsistency exists in the **class** names, tracked separately in #286 (higher blast radius, since those are rendered DOM classes).

title: Conversation history fails to save when a tool result contains an htmlwidget
description:
## Problem

When a tool result's `extra$display$html` contains an htmlwidget (e.g. a mapgl map), the widget renders correctly in the chat, but conversation-history persistence fails with a red toast:

> Could not save conversation: No method asJSON S3 class: htmlwidget

The save path (the `history_on_response` observer in `chat_history.R`, which calls `controller$on_response(get_turns_recorded(...))`) ultimately serializes the ellmer turns with `jsonlite::toJSON`, and the `ContentToolResult`'s `extra$display$html` holds the live htmlwidget object, which jsonlite cannot serialize.

## Repro

1. Register a tool that returns an interactive map:

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ellmer)
library(shinychat)
library(sf)
library(mapgl)

map_tool <- tool(
  function() {
    pts <- st_as_sf(
      data.frame(lon = runif(100, -125, -116), lat = runif(100, 32, 49)),
      coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326
    )
    map <- maplibre(style = carto_style("positron")) |>
      fit_bounds(pts, animate = FALSE) |>
      add_circle_layer(id = "pts", source = pts, circle_color = "#1b9e77")
    ContentToolResult(
      value = "Mapped 100 points.",
      extra = list(display = list(
        title = "Map", html = map, open = TRUE, full_screen = TRUE
      ))
    )
  },
  name = "show_map",
  description = "Show an interactive map of points."
)

ui <- page_fillable(chat_ui("chat"))
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  client <- chat_anthropic()
  client$register_tools(list(map_tool))
  chat_server("chat", client)  # history = TRUE (default)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

2. Ask: "Show me a map."
3. The map renders inline (great!), then the toast appears and the turn is not saved to history.

## Expected behavior

History persistence should either:

- Strip/skip non-serializable display content (e.g. drop `display$html` when it's an htmlwidget, or replace it with a placeholder) before saving, so the rest of the turn still persists, and/or
- Document that tools returning htmlwidgets are incompatible with `history = TRUE`, so app authors know to choose.

Ideally a restored conversation would show the tool card with a graceful fallback (title + text value) instead of failing the entire save.

## Environment

- shinychat 0.4.0.9000 (also reproduces against current `main` of posit-dev/shinychat — `chat_history.R` has no special handling for htmlwidgets)
- mapgl 0.5.0, ellmer (current), R 4.5.2, macOS

## Context

Hit while building a commons data agent whose custom `map_plots` tool returns mapgl htmlwidgets via `extra = list(display = list(html = ...))` — the htmlwidget-in-tool-card rendering works beautifully; only history save breaks.

title: Ship third-party license texts for the bundled JS assets
description:
## Problem

`pkg-py/src/shinychat/www/shinychat.js` (1.1 MB) is a prebuilt bundle that vendors third-party MIT-licensed code. From the esbuild legal-comments block at the end of the file:

| Bundled package | Copyright | License |
|---|---|---|
| `react`, `react-dom`, `scheduler`, `use-sync-external-store` | Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates | MIT |
| `use-stick-to-bottom` | StackBlitz | MIT |

esbuild names each package, which is good attribution, but the React headers say:

> This source code is licensed under the MIT license found in the **LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree**.

That's a pointer to a file we don't ship. The only license text in the sdist is `LICENSE` (shinychat's own MIT, Posit PBC). MIT requires the full license text and copyright notice to accompany redistribution, so the bundle as shipped is attribution without the text it points to.

To reproduce:

```
$ tar xzf shinychat-0.6.0.tar.gz
$ grep -A3 'Bundled license information' shinychat-0.6.0/pkg-py/src/shinychat/www/shinychat.js
```

## Why it's surfacing now

The conda-forge staged-recipes PR checklist ([`pull_request_template.md#L49`](https://github.com/conda-forge/staged-recipes/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md#L49)) says:

> Package does not vendor other packages. (If a package uses the source of another package, they should be separate packages or the licenses of all packages need to be packaged).

and the conda-forge docs section [Licenses of included dependencies](https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/adding_pkgs/#licenses-of-included-dependencies) says each vendored dependency needs its license file included in the recipe. Their tooling recommendations (`cargo-bundle-licenses`, `go-licenses`) are Rust/Go-specific; there's no equivalent guidance for bundled JS in a Python package, and enforcement is reviewer discretion. We are proceeding with [conda-forge/staged-recipes#34338](https://github.com/conda-forge/staged-recipes/pull/34338) as-is rather than blocking on this.

## Proposed fix

Emit a third-party license file during the JS build and ship it in both the sdist and wheel:

1. Collect license texts for the bundled deps at build time — e.g. a `license-checker-rspack` / `generate-license-file` step in `js/`, writing `THIRDPARTY.txt`.
2. Include it in the Python package alongside `LICENSE` (and in the R package if `pkg-r` ships the same bundle).
3. Verify it lands in the sdist: `tar tzf dist/shinychat-*.tar.gz | grep -i thirdparty`.

All bundled code is MIT, same as shinychat, so this is a compliance-hygiene fix rather than a licensing conflict.

## Release note / follow-through

Once a release ships `THIRDPARTY.txt`, **update the conda-forge feedstock** to reference it, so the vendored licenses are packaged in the conda artifact too:

```yaml
about:
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - THIRDPARTY.txt
```

The autotick bot bumps version and sha256 only — it won't add the new `license_file` entry, so this needs a manual edit to the bot's PR on `shinychat-feedstock` (or to `recipes/shinychat/recipe.yaml` in staged-recipes if that PR is still open at the time).

title: feat: stable conversation identity for R chat_server()
description:
ShinyChat currently creates `ConversationRecord$id` only after the first completed response is persisted. That is too late to correlate the model work that produced it with the saved conversation.



Expose a stable active conversation ID before managed model work begins, retain it through retries, restores, and switches, and record it on a ShinyChat response span. This gives Commons and similar audit or trajectory consumers a simple, history-store-independent way to identify the conversation a response belongs to without adding application context to ellmer.

<details>

<summary>Approved design plan</summary>

# ShinyChat stable conversation identity design

**Status:** Approved.

**Scope:** R ShinyChat's managed `chat_server()` path, plus the future Commons
telemetry-consumer contract.

## Purpose

ShinyChat already persists a stable ID on each `ConversationRecord`. That ID is
created too late for telemetry: the record does not exist until the first
completed response is saved, after the model call has finished.

This design moves conversation identity earlier in the lifecycle. A new
conversation receives an ID on its first user submission, before model work
begins. The same ID later becomes `ConversationRecord$id`.

ShinyChat exposes the active ID as application state and records it on an
OpenTelemetry span around managed responses. Commons can use that span to
group telemetry by the ShinyChat conversation the user actually selected.

## Goals

- Give a new conversation a stable ID before its first model call.
- Preserve that ID through failure, cancellation, retry, save, restore, edit,
  branch navigation, and client replacement.
- Expose the active ID through the object returned by `chat_server()`.
- Record the ID automatically around model work managed by `chat_server()`.
- Keep ellmer unaware of ShinyChat history identity.
- Let Commons prefer ShinyChat's saved-conversation identity while retaining
  its existing standalone fallback.

## Non-goals

- Add an exchange, response, message, or node ID.
- Model edit-branch lineage in Commons.
- Change `ConversationRecord` storage schema.
- Read ShinyChat's `ConversationStore` from Commons.
- Replay arbitrary ShinyChat UI state in a Commons trajectory.
- Add a public identity API for standalone `chat_enable_history()` users.
- Add Python parity in this work.
- Add compatibility behavior for unreleased telemetry.

## Current behavior

The R `HistoryController` uses `record = NULL` to represent an unsaved draft.
It creates the first `ConversationRecord` in `on_response()`, after the
browser has reported the completed assistant message:

```text
user submits
  -> ellmer model and tool work
  -> ShinyChat renders the response
  -> browser reports the completed messages
  -> HistoryController creates ConversationRecord$id
```

This timing is correct for saving UI state, but too late for correlating model
telemetry with the saved conversation.

`chat_server()` performs model work in an `ExtendedTask`. It currently passes
the client, UI ID, user input, and stream controller into that task. It does
not pass a history identity.

Commons independently allocates one conversation ID for the lifetime of its
client. A `commons_conversation_turn` span records that ID. When one Commons
client is used across restored or switched ShinyChat conversations, the
Commons ID does not identify the saved conversation.

## Terminology

- **Empty draft:** A new chat with no user submission. It has no ID.
- **Identified draft:** A chat that has received a user submission but has not
  yet been saved. It has an active conversation ID and no record.
- **Saved conversation:** A `ConversationRecord` whose `id` equals the active
  conversation ID.
- **Managed response:** Model work started by `chat_server()` in its built-in
  user-submission path.

## 1. Identity lifecycle

Conversation identity belongs to the active conversation, not to a completed
response or a storage write.

### Empty draft

Immediately after initialization or "New chat":

```text
active conversation ID = NULL
record = NULL
```

ShinyChat does not allocate or persist IDs for empty chats.

### First submission

Before invoking the model, `chat_server()` asks the current history controller
to ensure an active ID:

```text
active conversation ID = c_42
record = NULL
```

Repeated calls to ensure the ID return `c_42`. They never allocate another ID
for the same active draft.

### Failure, cancellation, and retry

A failed or cancelled model call does not clear the active ID. A later retry
or submission remains part of `c_42`.

The identified draft remains session-local until a response is saved. It does
not appear in the history store or drawer.

### First successful save

`HistoryController$on_response()` creates the first `ConversationRecord` with
the existing active ID:

```text
active conversation ID = c_42
record$id = c_42
```

`new_conversation_record()` must accept an explicit ID instead of always
allocating one internally.

### Restore and switch

Loading a stored record sets the active ID to `record$id` before another
submission can begin. Switching between records changes the active ID to the
selected record's ID.

A failed load leaves both the current record and active ID unchanged.

### Edit and branch navigation

Edits and sibling navigation change the active path inside one
`ConversationRecord`. They do not change the conversation ID.

### New chat and active deletion

Starting a new chat or deleting the active conversation clears the active ID
to `NULL`. The next user submission allocates a new ID.

### Client replacement

`chat$set_client()` re-registers history. It must carry the current active ID
into the replacement controller so the conversation does not become
temporarily unidentified.

If the active conversation already has a record, normal initialization
restores that record and confirms the same ID. If it is an unsaved identified
draft, the replacement controller inherits the draft ID without creating a
record.

## 2. Controller state and invariants

`HistoryController` gains reactive active-ID state separate from `record`.
The controller provides internal operations with these semantics:

- `conversation_id()` reactively returns one character ID or `NULL`.
- `ensure_conversation_id()` returns the current ID, allocating one when
  necessary.
- Activating a stored record sets both `record` and the active ID.
- Clearing the active conversation clears both `record` and the active ID.
- Seeding a replacement controller sets the draft ID without creating a
  record.

The central invariant is:

> When `record` is not `NULL`, the active conversation ID equals `record$id`.

Restore, switch, initialization, deletion, new-chat, and first-save paths must
use the shared controller operations. They must not assign `record` and active
identity independently.

The ID format remains the existing `c_`-prefixed value produced by
`new_conversation_id()`.

## 3. Public R API

The object returned by `chat_server()` gains:

```r
chat$history$conversation_id()
```

This is a Shiny reactive expression.

It returns:

- `NULL` when history is disabled,
- `NULL` for an empty draft,
- the identified draft ID after the first submission, and
- the stored record ID for a saved or restored conversation.

The reactive remains stable across history-controller replacement performed
by `chat$set_client()`. Internally, `chat_server()` keeps a reactive reference
to the current controller and delegates the public expression to it.

This design does not change the public return value of
`chat_enable_history()`. Standalone users do not receive a new identity API in
this work.

## 4. Managed submission flow

`chat_server()` changes its existing user-input observer:

1. Resolve the current history controller.
2. Call `ensure_conversation_id()` synchronously when history is enabled.
3. Capture the returned ID as a scalar.
4. Pass that scalar into the response `ExtendedTask`.
5. Open telemetry using only the captured scalar.

The task must not re-read `chat$history$conversation_id()` while it runs. A
history switch, new-chat action, or controller replacement must not relabel
in-flight work.

With history disabled, the captured ID is `NULL` and the task follows its
current uninstrumented path.

## 5. OpenTelemetry span

For a managed response with a conversation ID, ShinyChat opens one span:

```text
name: shinychat.response
kind: internal
attribute:
  gen_ai.conversation.id = c_42
```

The span begins before `client$stream_async()` and ends after `chat_append()`
has finished consuming the response stream. This lifetime places Commons,
ellmer model calls, and ellmer tool-loop spans beneath the same ShinyChat
response span.

Conceptually:

```text
shinychat.response                    gen_ai.conversation.id = c_42
└── commons_conversation_turn         gen_ai.conversation.id = commons-client-7
    └── ellmer chat and tool spans
```

The span name is fixed and low-cardinality. ShinyChat records no message
content, title, user identity, or rendered UI in its attributes.

The implementation uses `promises::with_otel_span()` so the active span
survives promise callbacks and closes after asynchronous stream consumption.
This requires:

- `promises >= 1.5.0`, and
- a direct `otel` package dependency for the ShinyChat tracer.

With no configured tracing provider, the wrapper is a no-op. ShinyChat must
not require an `otelsdk` provider or exporter.

ShinyChat emits no identity-bearing response span when history is disabled or
before an ID exists. Greeting generation and conversation-title generation
are not managed user responses and do not receive this span.

## 6. Commons consumption contract

Commons keeps its current client-lifetime conversation ID for standalone use.
It does not need to receive a new ellmer argument or read ShinyChat runtime
state directly.

When reconstructing trajectories, Commons resolves a chat span's conversation
identity in this order:

1. The nearest enclosing `shinychat.response` span carrying a valid
   `gen_ai.conversation.id`.
2. The current Commons wrapper's `gen_ai.conversation.id`.
3. The trace ID fallback.

This precedence is explicit because the inner Commons span already carries a
different value under the same semantic-convention attribute name.

The ShinyChat ID groups model and audit telemetry by saved conversation.
Commons' existing ID continues to group calls in apps that do not use managed
ShinyChat history.

This contract does not attach provenance by message or branch identity.
Conversation-level grouping and exchange-level audit association remain
separate concerns.

## 7. Failure and concurrency behavior

### Model failure or cancellation

The response span closes with the captured conversation ID. The active draft
ID remains available for retry. No history record is required.

### Store failure

A failed first store write does not allocate another ID. If the controller has
already constructed an in-memory record, it keeps that record and its ID even
though the conversation is not yet available from the store or history drawer.
The next valid save attempt persists the same record and ID.

The controller must preserve the identity invariant when record construction
succeeds but persistence fails.

### Restore failure

The existing load-before-mutate rule remains. ShinyChat changes neither the
current record nor the active ID when a target record cannot be loaded.

### Navigation during in-flight work

The response task uses the ID captured at invocation. Later reactive state
cannot change the span's identity.

This design does not otherwise change whether ShinyChat permits switching or
editing while a response is in flight.

### OpenTelemetry failure

Tracing is observational. Tracer creation, span activation, attribute
recording, or span closure must not prevent the model call or UI stream from
running.

## 8. Testing

### Controller unit tests

- A new controller has no conversation ID.
- `ensure_conversation_id()` allocates once and returns the same value on
  repeated calls.
- Failure or cancellation without a save retains the draft ID.
- The first saved record uses the preallocated ID.
- Later saves keep the same ID.
- Restore and switching adopt the stored record ID.
- Edit and sibling navigation retain the ID.
- New-chat and active deletion clear the ID.
- A failed switch leaves the current ID unchanged.
- A replacement controller inherits both saved and unsaved active IDs.
- Whenever a record exists, its ID equals the active ID.

### `chat_server()` integration tests

- `chat$history$conversation_id()` is initially `NULL`.
- The model client observes a non-`NULL` ID before its first managed call.
- The public reactive and eventual stored record report the same ID.
- Failed and retried calls report the same ID.
- Restoring and switching update the public reactive.
- `chat$set_client()` preserves the ID.
- With `history = FALSE`, the reactive remains `NULL`.

### OpenTelemetry tests

- A managed response produces one `shinychat.response` span when tracing is
  enabled.
- The span carries the captured `gen_ai.conversation.id`.
- Commons and ellmer spans are descendants of the response span.
- The span remains active through lazy stream consumption.
- Failure and cancellation close the span without changing its ID.
- History-disabled responses do not produce identity-bearing ShinyChat spans.
- Tracing-disabled responses behave identically to current chat responses.

### Future Commons integration tests

- Restore a saved conversation and continue it in a new session.
- Confirm the new spans group under the saved ShinyChat conversation ID.
- Switch between two saved conversations on one Commons client.
- Confirm the two trajectories remain separate even though the Commons
  fallback client ID is the same.
- Confirm standalone Commons still groups by its existing ID when no
  `shinychat.response` ancestor exists.

## 9. Expected file boundaries

ShinyChat R:

- `pkg-r/R/chat_history_types.R`: accept a preallocated record ID.
- `pkg-r/R/chat_history.R`: active-ID state and lifecycle operations.
- `pkg-r/R/chat_app.R`: public reactive, submission-time capture, controller
  replacement, and response span.
- `pkg-r/DESCRIPTION`: `promises` version floor and direct `otel` dependency.
- Existing R history and chat-server test files: controller, public API, and
  telemetry coverage.

Commons, in a later integration:

- `R/trajectory-read.R`: ShinyChat response-span identity precedence.
- Trajectory tests: restore, switching, and standalone fallback.

No JavaScript, ellmer, Python ShinyChat, or history-store migration is part of
this design.

## 10. Alternatives not selected

### Allocate a record only after the response

This is current behavior. It cannot identify the model work that creates the
first saved response.

### Allocate an ID when the user clicks "New chat"

This creates identities for empty abandoned drafts. Allocation on first
submission gives telemetry the ID in time without polluting history state.

### Use only a public reactive

This is explicit but does not automatically transport the ID to Commons inside
the managed model call. Apps could omit or mis-scope the integration.

### Use only an OpenTelemetry span

This transports identity but hides useful application state behind tracing.
The public reactive remains the source of truth; telemetry copies it.

### Add an ellmer request argument

Ellmer does not own ShinyChat history identity. Adding the argument would
broaden ellmer's API for context it does not otherwise use.

### Add a ShinyChat-to-Commons lifecycle hook

This avoids a general response span but creates a package integration protocol,
shared mutable context, and asynchronous cleanup requirements.

### Use Shiny's existing `ExtendedTask` span

That span is conditional on Shiny reactivity collection and is an internal
Shiny implementation detail. A named ShinyChat span provides a stable,
domain-specific boundary.

### Expose standalone `chat_enable_history()` identity now

There is no current consumer requiring a second public API. The internal
controller lifecycle can support that extension later without changing the
managed `chat_server()` contract.

## Success criteria

The design is successful when:

1. The first managed model call has a stable ShinyChat conversation ID.
2. The same ID survives retry and becomes the saved record ID.
3. Restore, switch, edit, branch navigation, and client replacement preserve
   the intended conversation identity.
4. `chat$history$conversation_id()` reports the active identity reactively.
5. Managed response telemetry carries the ID without changing ellmer.
6. Commons can prefer the ShinyChat ID and keep its existing standalone
   fallback.
7. No history store, JavaScript, Python, or message/node identity changes are
   required.
</details>

title: Greeting message is mis-ordered when restoring a conversation from history
description:
## Summary

If a chat starts with an assistant "greeting" message (via `chat_ui(messages = ...)`, `chat_append()`, or `chat_server(greeting = ...)`) and the user then has at least one real exchange, navigating away via the history navigator and back reorders the greeting so it lands *after* the user's first message instead of before it.

Expected order: `[greeting (A0), user (U1), response (A1)]`
Actual order after restore: `[user (U1), greeting (A0), response (A1)]`

## Repro app

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shinychat)
library(ellmer)

setClass(
  "ReproEchoProvider",
  representation(name = "character", model = "character")
)

make_echo_client <- function() {
  stored_turns <- list()
  client <- list(
    get_turns = function() stored_turns,
    set_turns = function(value) {
      stored_turns <<- value
      invisible(client)
    },
    get_tools = function() list(),
    get_provider = function() {
      methods::new("ReproEchoProvider", name = "Echo", model = "echo-test")
    },
    get_model = function() "echo-test",
    clone = function() make_echo_client()
  )
  class(client) <- c("Chat", "R6")
  client
}

record_exchange <- function(client, user_text, assistant_text) {
  turns <- c(
    client$get_turns(),
    list(
      UserTurn(contents = list(ContentText(user_text))),
      AssistantTurn(contents = list(ContentText(assistant_text)))
    )
  )
  client$set_turns(turns)
}

ui <- page_fillable(
  chat_ui(
    "chat",
    fill = TRUE,
    messages = list("Hi! I'm a greeting message."),
    placeholder = "Type a message"
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  client <- make_echo_client()

  chat_enable_history(
    "chat",
    client,
    options = history_options(
      store = "memory",
      scope = "repro-user",
      title = NULL
    )
  )

  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    user_text <- input$chat_user_input
    if (is.list(user_text)) user_text <- user_text[[1]]
    assistant_text <- paste0("echo: ", user_text)
    record_exchange(client, user_text, assistant_text)
    chat_append("chat", assistant_text)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Steps:
1. Load the app - greeting shows: "Hi! I'm a greeting message."
2. Send a message, wait for the echoed response.
3. Open the history navigator, click "New conversation".
4. Open the history navigator again, click back into the first conversation.
5. Observe the greeting is now the second message instead of the first.

Verified with a scripted shinytest2 run driving the actual history navigator UI (trigger button, "New conversation", conversation list item) - not just a code-level inference. Resulting order after restore: `["Tell me a joke", "Hi! I'm a greeting message.", "echo: Tell me a joke"]`.

## Likely culprit

The greeting is UI-only - it's rendered client-side and never becomes an ellmer turn (`chat_append()`, `chat_ui(messages = ...)`, and the `chat_server(greeting = ...)` machinery all funnel into UI-only message sends; `client$add_turn()` or equivalent is never called for it).

https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/2570b8d1025d5c7cc6a31a57c9e61129c4bc9e28/pkg-r/R/chat_history_types.R#L241-L323

`extend_record_linear()` builds one history-tree node per ellmer turn-group, then separately distributes the browser's reported UI messages onto those nodes:
- "user"-role UI messages are matched to the corresponding user-turn node.
- Everything else falls through to `fallback`, defined as the *last* newly created node.

Since the greeting has no backing turn, it's turn-less and gets swept into `fallback` - which, once a real exchange exists, is the node for the most recent assistant turn - rather than getting its own leading node. That's why it ends up appended right before/after the real response instead of staying in its original leading position.

Other relevant call sites:

https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/2570b8d1025d5c7cc6a31a57c9e61129c4bc9e28/pkg-r/R/chat_history.R#L76-L153

`on_response()` - supplies `recorded_turns` (ellmer turns only) and `messages`/`get_reported_messages()` (full UI list including the greeting) to `extend_record_linear()`.

https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/2570b8d1025d5c7cc6a31a57c9e61129c4bc9e28/pkg-r/R/chat_history.R#L235-L297

`replay_ui()` - walks the node path in order and flattens each node's `ui` list, which is where the reordering becomes visible.

https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/2570b8d1025d5c7cc6a31a57c9e61129c4bc9e28/pkg-r/R/chat.R#L734-L746

`chat_append()` - confirms the greeting never touches the ellmer client's turn history.

This isn't a persistence bug (the greeting *is* saved via `FileConversationStore$put()`) - it's a node-assignment bug in `extend_record_linear()`'s heuristic for placing turn-less UI messages. A fix likely needs to special-case UI messages reported before the first turn-bearing node (anchor them to a dedicated pre-turn/root node) rather than defaulting them to `fallback`. Leaving the exact approach open for whoever picks this up.

title: A stream that fails before its first yield is dropped, leaving a spinner that never resolves
description:
The error path in `chat_append_stream()` catches the rejection and appends `sanitized_chat_error(reason)` ([chat.R#L863-L887](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/64330fc2a703ea3bc005b221e42aace6389433ce/pkg-r/R/chat.R#L863-L887)). That only covers an error raised *after* `chat_append_stream_impl()` suspends at its first `await`. A provider that rejects the request outright fails before that, synchronously, so those handlers are never attached and nothing reaches the UI.

## Mechanism

The `ellmer::Chat$stream_async(stream = "content")` call returns a synchronous `coro_generator_instance`, and the request runs on its first advance — surfacing as a plain R error, not a rejected promise:

```r
client <- ellmer::chat_openai(
  base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1",
  model = "gpt-4.1-nano",
  credentials = function() list(Authorization = "Bearer x")
)

gen <- client$stream_async("hi", stream = "content")
gen()
#> Error in `req_perform_connection()`: Failed to perform HTTP request.
#> Caused by error in `open.connection()`: ! cannot open the connection
```

The consuming loop ([chat.R#L924](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/64330fc2a703ea3bc005b221e42aace6389433ce/pkg-r/R/chat.R#L924)) sits in the segment `coro::async()` runs eagerly, ahead of the first `await`. So the error propagates synchronously out of the *first* statement of `chat_append_stream()` ([chat.R#L856](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/64330fc2a703ea3bc005b221e42aace6389433ce/pkg-r/R/chat.R#L856)), skipping everything after it — both `promises::catch()` calls included. Tracing confirms it: `chat_append_message` is entered exactly once, for the `chunk = "start"`, and the `rlang::warn()` in the error handler never fires.

The error then lands in `append_stream_task`, whose result nothing reads — `on_stream_complete` branches only on `"success"`, and `status()` collapses `"success"` and `"error"` alike to `"idle"`, so a consumer cannot see it either:

```
task$status(): error | mod$status(): idle | result: httr2_failure: Failed to perform HTTP request.
```

The browser therefore keeps the loading bubble it raised on submit, with an empty `.shiny-chat-message-content` and `.shiny-chat-input` still carrying `disabled` — so the turn cannot be retried. Nothing later clears either: the `chunk = "end"` that would is in the handler that never runs.

This is the shape of every provider-side rejection — exhausted quota, over-long context, dropped connection, bad key. None yield a chunk, so none are the mid-stream case that is handled. A rejected turn is indistinguishable from a slow one, and the context-length case never recovers for the rest of the session.

## Reproducing

Nothing listens on port 1, so the first request is refused. Type anything and submit.

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinychat)

client <- ellmer::chat_openai(
  base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1",
  model = "gpt-4.1-nano",
  credentials = function() list(Authorization = "Bearer x"),
  echo = "none"
)

ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  chat_ui("chat"),
  verbatimTextOutput("probe")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  mod <- chat_server("chat", client, history = FALSE)

  task <- get("append_stream_task", envir = environment(mod$append))

  output$probe <- renderText({
    err <- tryCatch(task$result(), error = conditionMessage)
    paste0(
      "task$status(): ", task$status(),
      " | mod$status(): ", mod$status(),
      " | result: ", err
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Permalinks are pinned to 64330fc, which is what I ran; `main` is unchanged in all three respects ([chat.R#L991](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/main/pkg-r/R/chat.R#L991), [chat_app.R#L714](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/blob/main/pkg-r/R/chat_app.R#L714)). Versions: shinychat 0.4.0.9000 built from source, ellmer 0.4.1.9000, R 4.5.3.

## Fix

Turning the synchronous throw into a rejection routes these into the handling that already exists, since everything downstream of that line is promise-shaped:

```r
result <- tryCatch(
  chat_append_stream_impl(id, stream, role, icon, session),
  error = function(e) promises::promise_reject(e)
)
```

Applied to `chat.R:856` in a source build of 64330fc and re-running the app above:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| assistant bubble text | `''` | `An error occurred:` + the httr2 message |
| `.shiny-chat-input` has `disabled` | `TRUE` | `FALSE` |
| `chat_append_stream()` warning | absent | fires |

Note it deliberately leaves `chat_append_stream()` returning the rejected promise, so `append_stream_task$status()` stays `"error"`. Reading `append_stream_task$result()` in `on_stream_complete` is therefore still worth doing on its own — it would catch anything else escaping the append path and let a consumer tell a failed turn from a finished one, which `status()` currently cannot.

Happy to open a PR for either or both if that's useful — just say which you'd prefer.

Related to #276, but distinct: that asks for control over how a displayed error renders, and presumes it is displayed. This class is not displayed at all.

title: Reject unsupported conversation-history schema versions
description:
## Problem

Python and R conversation-history records include `schema_version`, currently version 1, but neither package validates the value before using the record. The file stores continue decoding records with any version, and `put()` can rewrite an existing record without first checking the on-disk version. A package version that encounters a record written by newer code could therefore misinterpret or overwrite it.

## Required behavior

Implement the guard concurrently in the Python and R packages with equivalent behavior:

- Define one authoritative supported record-schema version per package (currently `1`).
- Validate a record schema before version-dependent decoding in every history read path. Missing `schema_version` must continue to mean version 1 for compatibility with existing records.
- Reject unsupported versions with a clear compatibility error that reports the encountered and supported versions. Do not treat an unsupported schema as a generic malformed record.
- Validate records returned by custom `ConversationStore` implementations before the history controller uses them.
- Make writes fail closed:
  - reject an input conversation record with an unsupported version;
  - when `record.json` already exists, preflight its schema before initializing write state, appending JSONL data, touching files, or replacing `record.json`;
  - never overwrite an existing record whose schema is unsupported.
- Apply equivalent validation to each package's in-memory store or shared store boundary so an unsupported record cannot bypass the file-store checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Python and R `get()` and `list()` cannot decode a record with a schema newer than the package supports.
- Attempting to write a supported record over an existing unsupported record raises the compatibility error and leaves all files byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Attempting to write an unsupported record into an empty store fails without creating a conversation directory or files.
- A custom store returning an unsupported record is rejected before the record affects controller or client state.
- Existing version 1 records, including records without an explicit `schema_version`, continue to round-trip.
- Both package test suites cover unsupported reads, unsupported input writes, overwrite protection, custom-store ingress, and the legacy missing-version default.

## Out of scope

- Defining or migrating to a new record schema
- Changing the physical store layout
- General history-store refactoring

title: The `schema_version` guard is not enforced for custom `ConversationStore` implementations
description:
#312 / #313 added fail-closed rejection of unsupported conversation-record schema versions. That guard lives in the two built-in store implementations rather than at the interface or model boundary, so a third-party store that subclasses `ConversationStore` inherits none of it.

### Cause

In `pkg-py/src/shinychat/_history_store.py`, `ConversationStore` is an ABC whose abstract methods are `list`, `get`, `put`, `delete` — none of which check the version. Every `check_schema_version()` call site sits inside `FileConversationStore` or `InMemoryConversationStore`.

`pkg-r/R/chat_history_store.R` has the same shape: the exported `ConversationStore` R6 class contains only `rlang::abort("... must be implemented by subclass")` stubs, with the version checks in the two built-in subclasses.

The record models don't validate either:

```python
>>> from shinychat._history_types import ConversationRecord
>>> r = ConversationRecord(
...     schema_version=99, id="x", title="t",
...     created_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
...     updated_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
... )
>>> r.schema_version
99
```

So a custom store that reads JSON and constructs a `ConversationRecord` will happily return a record written by a future, incompatible version of shinychat.

### Impact

The practical consequence is that #312's compatibility boundary covers built-in stores only. Anyone implementing a store against a database or object store — the main reason the interface is public — gets no protection unless they know to call `check_schema_version()` themselves, which isn't currently documented as part of the contract.

### Possible directions

Not sure which is preferred, hence `enhancement` rather than `bug`:

1. Validate `schema_version` on the record model itself, so every construction path is guarded regardless of who built it.
2. Wrap the interface — have the calling layer check the version of whatever a store returns from `get()`/`list()`, so custom stores can't bypass it.
3. Leave enforcement to implementers but document it explicitly as part of the `ConversationStore` contract, and export `check_schema_version()` for them.

Option 1 is the most airtight and the smallest change, but note it would start rejecting out-of-range versions at construction time everywhere, including in test fixtures or user code that deliberately builds such a record. Option 3 alone would leave the boundary advisory.

### Related

Also worth documenting either way: an unsupported version currently fails `list()` for the **entire partition** rather than skipping the one record (`_history_store.py`, `chat_history_store.R`). That looks intentional — R has a comment explaining the deliberate capture-and-re-raise, and failing loudly avoids making a newer conversation look deleted — but the consequence isn't documented anywhere: one unreadable record disables the whole history list.

title: PDF attachments lose the user's filename before reaching ellmer
description:
In the R package, a PDF attachment's original filename is discarded before the content object is built, so the model receives a synthetic name like `file_001.pdf`. The Python package preserves the real filename. This is a cross-language behavior difference that affects live conversations, not just persistence.

### Cause

`content_from_attachment()` in `pkg-r/R/attachments.R` computes the attachment name and uses it for the text-attachment branch, but does not pass it to the PDF branch:

```r
content_from_attachment <- function(att) {
  mime <- att[["mime"]]
  data_url <- att[["data_url"]]
  name <- att[["name"]] %||% ""      # computed...

  if (startsWith(mime, "image/")) {
    return(ellmer::content_image_url(data_url))
  }
  if (identical(mime, "application/pdf")) {
    return(ellmer::content_pdf_url(data_url))   # ...but not used here
  }
  # ...text branch does use `name`
```

`ellmer::content_pdf_url()` has no filename parameter, so it substitutes `unique_pdf_name()`, a sequential `sprintf("file_%03d.pdf", counter)`. The real name is destroyed before the `ContentPDF` object exists — it isn't merely dropped at serialization time.

The Python path does the opposite, in `pkg-py/src/shinychat/_attachments.py`:

```python
if att.mime == "application/pdf":
    _require_data_url(att)
    data = decode_data_url(att.data_url)
    return ContentPDF(data=data, filename=att.name or "document.pdf")
```

### Reproducible example

```r
url <- paste0(
  "data:application/pdf;base64,",
  jsonlite::base64_enc(charToRaw("%PDF-1.4 fake"))
)

ellmer::content_pdf_url(url)@filename
#> [1] "file_001.pdf"
ellmer::content_pdf_url(url)@filename
#> [1] "file_002.pdf"
```

### Impact

The filename is part of the prompt context. A user who uploads `Q3-earnings.pdf` and asks "summarize the attached earnings report" gives the model a useful cue in Python and `file_001.pdf` in R. It also means the same app, ported between languages, sends the model different information.

### Suggested fix

Construct `ContentPDF` directly rather than going through `content_pdf_url()`, mirroring the Python branch. Verified this works:

```r
p <- jsonlite::base64_enc(charToRaw("%PDF-1.4 fake"))
ellmer::ContentPDF(
  type = "application/pdf",
  data = p,
  filename = "Q3-earnings.pdf"
)@filename
#> [1] "Q3-earnings.pdf"
```

A fallback of `"document.pdf"` when the name is empty would match Python exactly.

### Note

Image attachments lose their filename in **both** languages, because `ContentImageInline` has no filename field at all. That's an upstream limitation rather than a shinychat bug, so it's out of scope here — mentioning it only so the asymmetry isn't surprising.
